research_findings.headline: REQ-029 SOLVED with high confidence: the residual ~7% impossible top-5-holder sums trace to the PRODUCTION hard-block gate (degen_bot.py:1296-1349) using its OWN separate, broken exclusion logic instead of the already-correct Phase-1 resolver at line 5769 -- bonding-curve holders fail because the gate compares a per-mint PDA against the raw program ID one derivation hop too high, and graduated PumpSwap pools fail because RugCheck's markets[] doesn't enumerate every vault. All 8 RPC-forensically-sampled cases resolve to programs ALREADY in LP_OWNER_PROGRAMS -- this is a wiring bug, not a missing-program-ID gap, so the fix is a straight reuse of existing code. New hypothesis: bundle_supply_concentration_score -- a graded rug-risk signal (% of total supply distributed via the launch bundle) that goes beyond the bot's current boolean bundle_detected flag, using data the bot can already access via RPC with zero new paid APIs.

new_hypothesis.name: bundle_supply_concentration_score
new_hypothesis.mechanism: The bot currently treats Jito bundle detection as boolean (bundle_detected=True/False, already showing 20% WR vs 50% WR baseline). But launch bundles vary hugely in what fraction of total token supply they distribute to bundle-participant wallets in that one atomic transaction. A bundle that allocates 60-90% of supply across insider/decoy wallets is a fundamentally different (and more dangerous) structure than one that just seeds a small initial buy -- the former means insiders retain effective control of the float despite an apparently-distributed holder list, which is a strong precursor to a coordinated dump/rug that a boolean flag can't distinguish.
new_hypothesis.persistence: This requires parsing the actual per-wallet transfer amounts inside the bundle transaction against total supply at that block -- a continuous computation that off-the-shelf 'is this bundled' checkers (including the bot's current logic) do not expose. Because it needs bundle-internals parsing rather than a single API flag, it isn't a signal that gets arbitraged away by generic bundle-detection tooling; it stays a structural, non-priced-in read on insider control.
new_hypothesis.entry_rules: Phase-1 LOG-ONLY. For tokens the bot already flags bundle_detected=True, additionally fetch the bundle's constituent transaction(s) (via Jito Block Engine getBundleStatuses for the landed slot, or getParsedTransaction on the known bundle txids) and sum the token-transfer amounts routed to bundle-participant wallets; divide by total supply at that block to get bundle_supply_pct. Log this alongside existing trade features. No live filter change yet -- accumulate forward outcomes first.
new_hypothesis.data_required: Existing bundle-detection logic (bundle_detected boolean already computed) plus one additional getParsedTransaction / getBundleStatuses RPC call per bundled launch. Use ALCHEMY_SOLANA_RPC only -- no new paid API, no new external service.
new_hypothesis.evidence: Jito bundle-coordination subagent this run found that third-party bundle-risk tools (Trench Bot and similar) score bundles by supply-percentage distributed, not just presence/absence -- a graded axis the bot's current bundle_detected boolean does not capture. Confirmed free, no-auth Jito endpoints remain live (bundles.jito.wtf/api/v1/bundles/tip_floor, Block Engine getBundleStatuses). This is a genuinely unexplored angle: checked research-143 through research-151 history, no prior run examined bundle-internals supply-percentage (only the existing tip-floor regime signal and the boolean flag have been explored).

All 8 sampled impossible-sum cases (5 un-graduated bonding-curve, 3 graduated PumpSwap) resolve to programs ALREADY present in LP_OWNER_PROGRAMS -- no new program IDs needed, just reuse the existing correct resolver in the hard-block path.

proposals_for_survival_brain.expected_effect: Replacing the hard-block gate's exclusion logic at lines 1296-1349 with a call to self._get_holder_owner() + LP_OWNER_PROGRAMS membership (the same pattern already proven correct at lines 5769-5855) should drop the residual impossible-sum rate from ~7% toward ~0%, since every sampled failure mode maps to a program already in the existing allowlist.
proposals_for_survival_brain.kill_criteria: If a post-fix sample of N>=200 top5-holder checks (post-restart, new PID) still shows residual impossible-sum rate >=3%, the fix is incomplete -- reopen RPC forensics for a second failure class.

request_responses.finding: Root cause identified with high confidence via RPC forensics on 8 sampled impossible-sum cases. Case 1 (5/8, un-graduated bonding-curve tokens e.g. GmQDLfgm...pump, 5hRKdpPS...pump, logged at 100%): single top-1 holder resolves to a per-mint PDA owned by the pump.fun bonding-curve program (6EF8rrecthR5Dkzon8Nwu78hRvfCKubJ14M5uBEwF6P), but the hard-block gate's BONDING_CURVE comparison checks against the program ID directly, one derivation-hop too high, so it never matches. Case 2 (3/8, graduated PumpSwap tokens e.g. 7k4JoPp1...pump 101%, 2aQKC1xi...pump 106%, 8NGpdSE1...NCE 109%): holders resolve to the PumpSwap AMM program (pAMMBay6oceH9fJKBRHGP5D4bD4sWpmSwMn52FMfXEA, already in LP_OWNER_PROGRAMS), but RugCheck's markets[].liquidityA/liquidityB doesn't enumerate every PumpSwap vault variant, so the gate's secondary RugCheck-based path also misses them. Both failure classes exist because the production hard-block gate (degen_bot.py:1296-1349) uses its own independent, narrower exclusion logic instead of calling the already-correct _get_holder_owner()/LP_OWNER_PROGRAMS resolver used at lines 5769-5855. Proposed fix delivered in proposals_for_survival_brain (reuse the existing resolver, no new program IDs required).
